utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that both parties had preliminary -- Prosecution wants to raise, I think, three preliminary matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honours. Thank you very much. The first matter relates to Exhibit D316. There was a problem with the English translation, and now we'd inform the Chamber that we have uploaded the correct English translation as doc ID 0320-2965-ET-1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Madam Registrar is instructed to replace the current translation for D316 with the new uploaded one bearing doc ID number 0320-2965-ET-1.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Secondly, pursuant to the Trial Chamber's decision on the Prosecution motion to admit evidence from the bar table relating to the Foca municipality dated 14 November 2013, at paragraph 17, the Prosecution advises that the redaction of the English translation has been fixed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That document is 65 ter 08429A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if I remember well, it was a condition for admission, if I --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it's hereby on the record that the condition has been fulfilled. Unless there's any -- I take it that the Defence will have a look at it and can revisit the matter within the next 48 hours if there's anything to -- to -- to raise about this. Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would finally like to inform the Chamber of the following: In examining the materials the Defence intends to put to the witness, Dr. Tabeau, we conducted some additional searches. We identified a document which provides some potential additional information regarding six of the victims analysed in Dr. Tabeau's POD project. The document was disclosed to the Defence originally in batch 4 as Rule 68(ii), and upon our discovery of the document on Friday on that same day we disclosed it again as Rule 68(i), in relation to Dr. Tabeau. Although the document is not final in its conclusions regarding thighs six victims, the document does raise the possibility that there may be additional information possessed by ICMP which may impact upon the results obtained by Dr. Tabeau in her analysis in relation to those six. The Prosecution, therefore, would like to inform the Chamber and the Defence that we are planning to send a request to the ICMP asking them, as a matter of urgency, to provide us with any documentation they may have in relation to these six victims. Thereafter --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpreters, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Apologies. Thereafter, the Prosecution will ask Dr. Tabeau to re-analyse these six victims if there was anything in the ICMP response that impacts upon the victims. In any case, we will keep the Chamber and the Defence fully informed. If the material does result in any amendment to the analysis, we will inform the Chamber and seek to tender that additional analysis or file it as a written submission as the Chamber prefers. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any submission at this moment about that? Because, Ms. Marcus, it would not come as a great surprise if the Defence would come with untimely adding materials and untimely further investigations. So if you say, What the Chamber prefers, as far as tendering is concerned, the Chamber might first want to hear the Defence on the matter. Not necessarily immediately, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can confirm that we did receive, I believe on Friday or Saturday, the document in question and I have glanced at it. I do not know -- I have not been able to check to see whether it was in batch 4 or not so I have nothing that I can say in that regard at present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, the Prosecution is free to proceed as it wishes, and if it has any results to present them in court and then we'll find out what will happen with those results. Apart from that, the Chamber has no idea, of course, what the document is about, whether it's a 200-page complex document or a one-page simple document. This being on the record, I think nothing prevents us from continuing to hear the testimony of Ms. Tabeau in cross-examination. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Tabeau. Before we continue, I'd like to remind that you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Ivetic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Last week we left off talking about Dr. Patrick Ball and hacktivism, and I'd like to just raise with you the issue noted by Judge Orie last week and ask you to explain to us if your view of hacktivism which you were talking about included the aspect of illegal hacking to promote a social cause which was the subject of the -- or was implied in the article relating to Dr. Ball.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I gave you an example of what my understanding is of this so-called hacking process. In my understanding, and I spoke about it with Patrick Ball, it is more about streaming the energy of this young talented people into processes that are positive and beneficial to the society instead of illegal hacking into governmental systems and acquiring illegally information that is not meant for public use. So, once again, young people with skills can use their energy to -- for processes that can be good for the society. And that is my understanding of the hacking idea that Patrick Ball addressed to me at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I say that you spoke with Patrick Ball and that he addressed the idea to you. Would that have been before the drafting of the reports in this case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain what idea exactly you're referring to, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Page 5, line 8, where she said: It is my understanding of the hacking idea that Patrick Ball addressed to me at that time. My question is in relation to that. At what time was that? Was it before the drafting of the reports in this case.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was in touch with Patrick Ball on the occasion of writing a report acquired -- authored from us in relation to the Mirsad Tokaca database on the victims of the war in Bosnia. It was many years ago. I don't recall exactly the date but long before I was working on this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you believe that it is appropriate for demographic practitioner to make value judgements or advocate a particular legal or political position in their demographic reports, or do you believe that such demographic reports need to be clinical and scientific in nature, just presenting the facts and not advocating a position?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I think there are many different types of demographic reports and there is a need to make a distinction for -- between the reports that are made for use in the courts of law from reports that are meant for other purposes, scientific articles, yeah, articles by demographers in normal media, in the press. I think it is important to separate yourself as a demographer from any speculation and unjustified views in reports that are made for court, and, generally, it is important not to speculate but base your work and articles, reports on -- on good reasons, on a good foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to 1D1437 in e-court, and page 37 of the same. This will correlate to transcript page 21927 of the Prlic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can focus on lines 16 and forward, I'd like to ask you to follow along as I read into the record the testimony at that time: "Q. Very well. Then tell me: In the field of demography, what is the definition of siege? "A. There is no definition of siege within the field of demography and -- "Q. What about ethnic cleansing? What is the definition of ethnic cleansing within the field of demography as applied by your colleagues? "A. Well, I don't think there is a definition of ethnic cleansing in demography. "Q. Whose idea was it, ma'am, to use the term 'internally displaced persons' or 'refugees' as you have done in your report to identify," if we can go to the next page, "people who moved within the country or moved outside the country, irrespective -- irrespective of the reasons? Whose idea was it? "A. Whose idea was it? "Q. Yes. "A. We just used the term in order to make it clear that we are trying to statistically measure the displacement and we believe that is the best term to resemble this idea. Well, I wouldn't be able to tell you who figured out that this term should be used. We have been using this term since the very beginning of this project." Is this testimony accurate and truthful, so that you would testify the same way today.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the current versions of your reports, do they -- they -- they use words like "massacre," "atrocity," "victimisation." Could you consider that those are appropriate words to use in a demographic report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this transcript, you just read, there is no use of words like "massacre," "atrocity," "victimisation." It is the term internally displaced persons and refugees that were used. So this is one thing and I confirm I would use these terms again today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understand that, madam and I have moved on to another question asking you about you about the terms "massacre," "atrocity," "victimisation." And I asked are those appropriate words to use in a demographic report.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can give me, again, explanation what are you talking about, I can take a position on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm using the terms "massacre," "atrocity," and "victimisation" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, it's clear that Ms. Tabeau seeks context for the question in relation to her work, and I think it's fair to provide it to her. So apart from starting with the -- let's -- let's get to concrete moments where she -- as you suggest, she used those terms so that she can express herself on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, if we can look at 65 ter 11269.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That's P1900, Your Honour, just to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can turn to page 14 of the same. The second-to-last paragraph uses the term "massacre."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So let's take them one by one. Do you believe that the use of the term "massacre" in a demographic report is appropriate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The word of "massacre" is used in the second-last paragraph. It is used in the 2009 Srebrenica report. That is related to about 8.000 individuals who went missing during the fall of Srebrenica and subsequently a large number of them were exhumed from mass and other graves in the territory of Srebrenica and neighbouring municipalities. And subsequently a large number of them were identified through DNA analysis, and in this way the circle closed. I think this is very good reason, in my eyes, to call Srebrenica and victims of the fall of Srebrenica a massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My question was: In a demography sense do you think it is professionally appropriate to use the term "massacre" in a demographic report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is it no demography sense in general. We can talk about a report like Srebrenica report, about victims of the fall of Srebrenica, and in this context, this term is used very appropriately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 22. The heading of the section 2.5, is entitled: "The scale of victimisation of the fall of Srebrenica." And that word "victimisation" is used again on page 23, the following page. Do you believe it is appropriate in a demographic report to use terminology like "victimisation"?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular demographic report it is used very appropriately. It -- again, because the report itself is about the victims of the fall of Srebrenica, large number of individuals that were confirmed to be killed in a violent way and their bodies were exhumed from mass and other graves in the territory of Srebrenica and surrounding municipalities. And, again, identified through DNA analysis, et cetera, et cetera. So we are speaking of the same report, of the same situation, and it is fully justified to speak about the scale of victimisation in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 24. At the top, the first paragraph underneath the first table uses the term "atrocities." Same question: Do you consider it appropriate in a demographic study to use the term atrocities?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the same answer. It is, again, the same report, the same situation. We are dealing with missing persons, exhumation materials related to their death. A lot of other evidence exists that describes what happened. So I think it is, again, the same answer: It's appropriate to use this term.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, is it correct, ma'am, that the use of these terms by your office was the result of hearing those words in the media and wanting to reflect what was in the media?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not true, of course. I haven't used -- we haven't used any media reports to make our Srebrenica reports. We based our analysis on sources like missing persons records, DNA identification reports, exhumation records. I wouldn't call any of these sources a media report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What about for prior cases, did you use media reports to come up with terminology to be used in your reports?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, I never used media reports as a source for any demographic report related to victims of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get back to that. Let's turn to the tasking by the Prosecution and the methodology that you employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have 1D1440 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this will be the transcript of your testimony from the Zupljanin and Stanisic case, and it will be at page 19 that we need to go, which will be transcript page 15513 of that underlying case. If we could zoom on the line 9 and following: "Q. What type of demographics do you deal with? What is your speciality, so to speak? "A. Before I answer this question, please, sir, I would like to draw your attention to Annex B2 of the addendum. The title of this annex is 'Comparison of the Stanisic and Zupljanin case area with Bosnia and Herzegovina.' Here, can you find the contextual statistics for Bosnia in this section. "Now, going back to the field of demographics I deal with, I deal with general demography, I think, and in particular, I was specialised years long in the study of mortality in developed countries, mostly countries of Western Europe, Central Europe, and some East European countries, and I studied life expectancy. So it is mortality, generally speaking. "Now, the experience from the ten last years from this Tribunal it would be most certainly war demography. This is a new area in demography which is quite different from classical demography of western counties or classical demography of another type. But that would be the two," if you could go to the next page, I believe "areas, the study of mortality in developed countries on one hand, and, in addition to this, demography of war. "I think there's a correction needed in the transcript, last line. It was 'demography of war' I said in the end. This is page 19, row 14. Demography of war. Thank you. "Q. And you have worked on war demographics ever since your collaboration with the OTP began. Sorry, I apologise. You deal with war mortality issues since you began working with the OTP. "A. Not only war mortality. If you look at what I have done here in this Tribunal, there is a study of population displacement, internal and external, a lot of reports on that. There would be these two subjects. War mortality and forced migration, I would call it, internal and external." Do you stand by this testimony as being truthful and accurate, such that you would testify the same way if asked these questions today?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, this discussion raises a topic I'd like to discuss with you, mortality studies, or I think they're also called morbidity studies. Would you agree with me this aspect of your field involves determining mortality statistics to estimate the average number of persons that would become deceased in a year due to a variety of causes including natural death, illness, traffic accidents, suicides, as well as murders, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, generally I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you: Such studies and statistical figures are performed by people in the same field as you for every country and every time-period such that they would be available for other demographers or statisticians to utilise; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, among other things, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Such mortality figures would vary from country to country, region to region, based on the unique factors in that area which affect such things, size of population, environmental factors, health care availability, things like that; is that also accurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, among other things, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relations to the reports that you were asked to prepare in this case by the Office of the Prosecutor did you utilise any of the standardised and known mortality figures and statistics for either the Balkans or for Bosnia-Herzegovina? Did you incorporate the same into your studies to account for numbers of persons that would normally be expected to become deceased even if nothing else was going on?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually I did. In one of the Sarajevo reports I made a reference to observe mortality rates for the Sarajevo area in certain period. Well, it is not, first of all, always necessary to make such comparisons and sometimes it simply doesn't make sense to -- to compare natural mortality with war mortality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, what about your report on the population changes in the -- in 22 municipalities. Do you think that mortality studies would have had a role relevant to that study?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What role? What do you mean? What kind of role that mortality could play in estimating population movements?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you think that mortality statistics have a role when you're reporting upon population changes in a particular area?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, these reports, IDP's report -- IDP's and refugee report for the Mladic case area had a subject of estimating the minimum numbers of IDPs and refugees and these numbers were produced. So in this particular report, no rates were presented of migration. If I would be estimating rates then I would be thinking of all contributing factors to the estimation of the rates. But it was not the subject of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. What about in the Srebrenica reports? Were there mortality rates or statistics used in the preparation of those reports and those opinions?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you might recall, there is a section in the integrated report of 2009 where certain relative measures are presented, these are the ratios, mortality ratios, not the rate, but ratios that have been estimated and are discussed. So also in the Srebrenica report, there is a short discussion of the relative measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that for traditional demographic studies there is a well defined methodology to estimate the sampling variance of the proportions involved so as to arrive at a margin of error?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But, first of all, I don't understand why are you insist on comparing traditional studies with war demographics studies. That is one thing as we agreed, and I said in the other case, and it is on the transcript that war demography is not necessarily the same area of -- as the classical demography is, that is one thing; and, of course, we can always calculate variance for rates and probabilities that are being produced. But why we would do that for Srebrenica? I'm asking. What kind of variability you want to discuss? It is the ratios that are calculated for the actual observed persons who went missing from Srebrenica. So it is a measure that expresses the very fact of going missing in terms of relative value and no more than that. It -- we are not talking of a sample of Srebrenica victims, as a matter of fact. We made an effort to count them all, and we have been doing this for a very long time, for more than ten years, in order to count them all and the ratios calculated in the Srebrenica are presented for the counts of missing persons that are almost complete. These are very good counts. These are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you continue, it seems that the basic disagreement or misunderstanding seems to be that demographic reports based on samples and then to draw conclusions from samples for the totality is something that was not at all used in your reports. Mr. Ivetic, if you could either explain to the Chamber or make clear in questions, follow-up questions, why you think that sampling is relevant where Ms. Tabeau tells us and it's clear from her reports that no sampling at all was done, then the Chamber would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may add, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sampling methods were used in the IDPs and refugees report when next to the minimum number of IDPs and refugees also an estimated number is presented, the more complete estimated number of the IDPs and refugees. And in this case, of course, there is the variance analysis included in the form of presenting confidence intervals for these counts. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, if I understand the reports well their sampling is based on a totally different basis than what you usually, I would say, in the normal demographic reports that you find a kind of sample which suits your methods best, whereas here it was more or less -- more or less imposed by the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely right. It was not random sampling --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- picking up a sample according to certain procedures. The purpose has always been in every report to produce the count, the counts and not work with sample data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In relation to the sources that are used in any demography study, would you agree that the quality of the outcome depends on the quality of the sources?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, quality of the sources is very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. The methodology which you used for purposes of your various reports am I correct that it is, in part, based on a concept in demography called exploitation of links?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We used linkage of records as the foundation for the methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when I used the term "exploitation of links," I mean when I want to take a census from one year and then compare it with the census of another year, or if I want to take the census for one municipality and compare it to another municipality, if there is more than one link with more than one source of information, I have to uses a precise key to do this. When I need an exploitation of links it is because of multiple links due to the quality of information and that means that I'm not using a single key and constantly shifting this exploitation and these links. Do you agree with -- is that the -- in essence the meaning behind "exploitation of links" in a demography sense?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I cannot agree with what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Linking is a simple thing, just, you know, comparing related records into sources and deciding whether the similarity of these two compared records is good enough to declare them representing one the same case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with the statement that as a demographer you cannot reliably exploit more than one link in a single source of information?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if there is a single source of information, we don't talk about linkage of records because there is no other source with which this source could be linked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that as one needs the exploitation of multiple links due to the quality of the information that is essentially when you need many different keys or criteria to successfully match or compare two sets of data?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, I don't know exactly what you are talking. Perhaps you are referring to the criteria of linking. Well, one can do it based on a single numerical characteristic like record ID, if this characteristic is the same in two compared records. One can do it also based on other criteria like descriptive items included in the record, like names, date of birth, other characteristics. So it is still linking records, two records in two related sources of information but just based on different criteria.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the answer is again and again that Ms. Tabeau is guessing what you are meaning with very abstract questions. And that, therefore, she has some difficulties in answering them. Why not be concrete and say, You used this system here, that and that and that, would it not have been appropriate to use a different method there because this one is flawed for that and that reason, then we know what are you talking about, apart from very abstract statements about methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, in application of expertise, one had to go to the abstract and the study itself and to see what types of concepts are common amongst other professionals in that same field of study, and that's what I'm trying to do. And I'm using terminology that I believe is very precise in that field of study.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then, at a certain moment you have to link it to the evidence which is before this Chamber. I mean, disagreed about methods used or not used is not the core issue of this case. The core issue of this case is the way in which the report was drafted, on what basis it was drafted, what method it uses, and then, finally, we have to come to the report, not to remain in the abstract area. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's use your term for it, "criteria." Would you agree that with an increase in the number of criteria needed to identify a match, the confidence rating or factor of the data you receive would be lowered?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. So if you could re-phrase, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me re-phrase it in another way. Are you familiar with the concept of statistical overview?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does it mean to you the statistical overview? There are many overviews, statistical overviews, that one can make.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm using the term "statistical overview" in the sense of when using such a large number of criteria it would be appropriate to give a statistical overview as to how many cases you linked using one criteria, how many cases you linked varying two characteristics, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what is this large number of criteria you are referring to? If you could give it to me. I don't understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The criteria -- I used keys, [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Large number [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- you used criteria. Were over 70 criteria used in the Srebrenica report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, these. Yeah. Well, this is -- now I finally got what you are asking about. The criteria, 70 criteria to use too much the records of Srebrenica victims with the census; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you referring to. Yes. In this context you would like to know whether the fact that we used that main criteria has lowered or improved the quality of matching; right? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My question was: First of all, would you agree that with the increase in the number of criteria necessary for a match whether the confidence rating or confidence factor in that particular conclusion is lowered.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- I would disagree with you. It is, I think, a misperception of how the criteria were used in the process of matching. If -- if there is no numerical record ID in every source match, then one has to turn to use descriptive data items in the matching process. Indeed, I at some point presented a list of the criteria used based on this descriptive items, but it doesn't mean that all these criteria had to be applied, all the 70 or 90 or whatever, in order to get a match. So this is a list that gives ideas about what kind of requirement were requested by those who were doing the matching, in order to declare a true match. For instance, if first name, surname, father's name and the date of birth were identical in two records matched, then a number of records were taken as confirmed and matched and declared as true matches. However, this number didn't comprise all the records that could and should be matched. So in the next step, we move to another criterion. We had to allow for the differences in the spellings of names. Instead of comparing full names, first name, father's name, surname, one can require that 75 per cent of the characters in the first name, surname, father's name are consistently the same, between the two records compared, plus the date of birth. That means that we allow for 25 per cent of spelling differences in the names. So, after the first criterion, based on complete names, one moves to the next criterion, based on 75 per cent of characters the same in two compared records. And there will be a small group of records that could be found identified as the same and declared true matches. However, there are also mistakes in the dates of birth. So in the next step, one would allow as well for differences in reporting the date of birth and say that the year must be the same but the month can be slightly different. Plus minus one, two, year, for instance. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you there. Was it plus or minus five years your standard?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not standard. There were different queries, with different restrictions related or conditions related to the year of birth. In some cases you are absolutely right. Even a five-year difference was allowed. That is very correct. And this is because the reporting of dates is very bad in sources that are not based on documents like identification cards from which the actual accurate date can be taken for reporting. So this list of 70 criteria is a list of subsequent steps that are taken in the matching process in order to find as many records representing the same individuals in both sources as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that it is the job of the demographer or statistician to keep track of the percentage of matching once you deviate from the original key so as to give a statistical overview of how many matches were found using the first criteria, how many matches were found using the second criteria, how many matches were found with the third, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ideally we would like to have such statistics, absolutely. But if you think of how many millions of records had to be reviewed in this kind of procedures and how many matches first indicated as potential matches, then assessed and then rejected, or partly accepted, and so on and so on, it is a process that have been continued years and years long, since the beginning of the Demographic Unit. So keeping these kind of statistics would eat up a lot of our time, if not all of it, you see, and there was also other work to do in this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now for purposes of all of your reports you have utilised as a starting point the 1991 census for the areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Apart from your participation in a population census in Poland as a student, is it correct that you -- that you did not take part in the organisation or the taking of any other census data?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't take part in any other census. I also didn't participate in the compilation of voters' register. I didn't participate in ICRC project in which they collected records of the missing persons from the families of the missing. I didn't participate in the work of statistical authorities, collecting information about death notifications, and so on and so on. I think that there is no need for everybody to participate in making of every source we ever use for our work. There are documents describing the compilation of sources and it is possible to study how the sources were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you consider to be a technical expert on the conduct of census in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not an expert in -- on the conduct of census, not in Bosnia, not in other country. I am just knowledgeable and familiar with the procedures and the methodology of how censuses are made.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to 1D1435 in e-court. And page 19 of the same. This should correlate with transcript page 6459 of the Stakic proceedings. And if we can focus on lines 9 through 18. The question and answer are recorded as follows: "Q. Before we get into the actual errors within the names, what my concern initially and what my question in part was, the census controls that were missing in Bosnia-Herzegovina, so that I may have a better understanding, would they be things that would include like a pilot survey or a sample survey, which are two distinction things, though; correct? "A. Yes. Now, usually before the census starts, there is a pilot, or -- a pilot census, microcensus, in which the questionnaire is tested and possible mistakes are detected and conclusions from this pilot are used in this census itself. As far as I know there was no pilot or additional surveys."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you stand by this testimony as being accurate and truthful. There was no pilot survey done before the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually was wrong, if I really said so, because there was a pilot census in Bosnia-Herzegovina before the 1991 census actually took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that you only found out about the pilot survey sometime in 2002?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I wouldn't recall exactly when, but at some point, indeed, more information was collected about the pilot census from the authorities who actually were involved in it. I wouldn't recall exactly the date. It was in early years of my employment at the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And prior to discovering the existence of the pilot census, you had already begun working with the census and drafting, I believe, at least one report on the matter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it might have been the case. But -- okay. That -- that's my answer, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see we're at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I could ask one question. If you would have known at the time that there had been a pilot, would that have in any way impacted on a report which you drafted before having that knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course not, because pilot is never used together with the actual census data. It is a pre-census survey, relatively small survey, in which the questionnaire is actually tested. So I -- in terms of data or knowledge from the pilot, there is nothing that could be -- have been used in any of the reports I made using the census data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can imagine that if you have assessed or expressed views on the reliability of the census, the -- that whether or not there have been a pilot may have some impact on the -- such an assessment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the pilot is namely -- predominantly to test the survey questionnaire and the questions in the census are very standard. So it is about details of the questionnaire, like the place of the question, you know, how to ask the question. And the experience from the pilot is used to improve the questionnaire but also to improve the training of the actual interviewers that later participate in asking the questions, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is aimed at improving the quality of the results of the census. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- how I have to understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take a break and after Ms. Tabeau has been escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be brought in, Ms. Marcus, the Chamber has considered whether it makes any sense at this moment to already assign preliminary numbers to the Brown materials, but the Chamber doesn't think that it speeds up considerably. So, therefore, let's do it the usual way, as always, also, in view of the fact that these are relatively small numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, yes, associated exhibits is a different matter. There are quite a few. That's always -- gives -- is of some concern to the Chamber but I'm not -- I'll not elaborate on that at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could you just clarify, please, Your Honour, if you would want that tendering to be done after the initial -- after the 92 -- in the initial process or after the conclusion of the witness's direct examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think, usually if it is put to the witness then we assign a number and usually the Chamber decides almost always at the end of the cross-examination for all of it. Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to revisit an area that we discussed earlier in relation to whether you had used media reports as a source for any demographic report related to victims of war as to terminology in -- that was at temporary transcript page 10, lines 9 through 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd now call up 1D1437 in e-court and ask for page 39 of the same, which should correlate to transcript page 21929 of the Prlic case. And if we could focus on lines 22 and onward.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you could follow along, please: "Q. Thank you. Thank you, ma'am. Now with respect to siege, what is your definition of siege, number one. I'm asking a compound question. But, number two, how is it that you determined, you, the demography, that indeed what was happening in Mostar at that conflict it was a siege or was this something that you decided to use, sort of, for convenient purposes? "A. Well, I didn't use it for convenient purposes. I rather follow the common definition, definition, or common use, say better. Well, in many press reports, videos, from this period the term 'siege' is used and there is no other connotations behind my use of this term. I just took it from the common use in the media in this period. "Q. Okay. I take it you believe what you read in the media? "A. Well, I don't. "Q. Yes or no. "A. This is not a yes and no question. "Q. Okay, very well. "A. The quality of information in the media is very different, very, very different, and there is no reason to trust everything you hear in the media. "Q. Is there anything in your report where you qualify the term 'siege' or 'ethnic cleansing' to suggest, at least to the Court, trying to be an objective and impartial and a [sic] expert witness that you are using these terms merely because this is something that you read in the press versus, say, the impression that I got from reading your report that you believed that there was a siege and that there was ethnic cleansing? Is there anywhere in your report where you -- where you alert the reader as to your intentions behind using these particular terms? "A. Well, there is no definitions of the terms 'siege' and 'ethnic cleansing,' you are right. There's no definitions as such, but -- well, I am surprised you are talking about it as the ethnic cleansing is a term that has been used also in many legal documents in the Statute of this Tribunal. "Q. Really? "A. Yes, really it is. "Q. There's a crime called ethnic cleansing, as far as you know? "A. Okay, there's no definition in my report. Are you happy? "Q. But you would agree with me, ma'am, that it's not your job to determine whether ethnic cleansing occurred, assuming that it did happen, and we know what it is, or that a siege was taking place. That is not your job. Your job is to deal with figures and statistics; correct? "A. Yes, it is. But as far as I remember, I didn't make any -- in my final conclusions, any statements related to the fact that there has been ethnic cleansing, there has been siege, and what is the meaning of this." Does this refresh your recollection as to the use of terminology gleaned from the -- their usage in the media for the purposes of reports that you authored for this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the transcript you just read refers to the definition of -- of siege and ethnic cleansing. And as such, as I said, I haven't defined these terms in my report. I rather use the term of 'siege' in common sense, that is how it was used, and always has been in any reports that I made, just a common-sense understanding of the term siege. That is one thing. Using of media as a source would mean that I used media reports on victims to make statistics on victims of the siege of Mostar. I haven't done this, and I haven't done this in other reports as well. So, in this sense, I have not used media as a source for my report. But other than that, we all, of course, read press and listen to television, and we -- we just use media reports in everyday life. It is quite a normal situation. This is what I do as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Getting back to where we've started, we were talking about terminology and we're talking about the victimisation of Srebrenica. The use of the term "massacre" and the use of the term "atrocity" in your integrated Srebrenica report, were those terms gleaned from the media and inserted as a result of hearing them in the media?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, it was not the case. It was not following the media in calling Srebrenica victims victims or that there was a massacre. All the sources that were used for the report indicated this fact very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, last week in the slide presentation that the Prosecution used during your direct examination, in one of the slides, I believe it was number 5, you had info on fallen soldiers among the three main warring factions. I would like to switch gears and talk about all casualties. First, can you tell us if there is a generally accepted source or sources of information documenting the total number of war-time casualties in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I myself made a source, if I can say, call it a source, through compiling, merging a number of original sources. The integrated database was established from which a number was produced of all victims of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. There exists also another source. This is the database on war victims that was compiled by Mirza Tokaca in Sarajevo by the Research and Documentation Centre in Sarajevo. They also have their own number of the victims of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And, of course, there are other numbers produced at various occasions by other authors, even at some point made an overview of the estimate of war victims available for Bosnia and Herzegovina so there are -- there are numbers. There exist numbers on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based on your research and knowledge, can you confirm for us that when looking at the war-time casualties as a percentage of the total population of a particular ethnic group, the Bosnian Serbs were the highest percentage of their population as war-time casualties some 2.6 per cent of their population was lost as opposed to 2.3 per cent of the Bosnian Muslim population and 2 per cent of the Bosnian Croat population?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would really feel comfortable if we would have this fragment from my article on the screen. It might be so that there were these kind of small differences among the ethnic groups. But I don't recall the exact percentages, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could council kindly speak closer to the microphone, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I want to now to switch gears to talk about the Srebrenica reports. In relation to your department's work in this area, in relation to the start of the hostilities in July 1995, the attack on Srebrenica began 6 July 1995 and lasted until 11 July 1995. Do you know the exact number of casualties on the side of the Bosnian Muslim defenders of Srebrenica; that is, the number of person who died as part of the combat undergoing the attack during those first few days, 6 July to 11 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we all know, there are no distinctions between combatants and non-combatants that we made in our reports on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know, based upon your research, do you have any data as to the precise number of individuals that would have become deceased as part of the trek of the column of Bosnian males that left Srebrenica and went through the forest, engaged in fighting with the Serb, going through mind fields, committing suicide, and killing each other. Do you have any data on either the precise number, ranges, anything?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the precise number and these causes that you mentioned, going through minefields, committing suicide, killing each other. Of course, I don't have information about that. It's not in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you accept that the bodies of those casualties, albeit the number you don't know, must be included in your figures of missing and even amongst some of those exhumed?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I didn't study the causes, specific causes for every Srebrenica victim, so I cannot comment on that. And, well, I can tell is that a very large per cent of the missing persons related to the fall of Srebrenica were buried in unmarked graves, many of them being mass graves, that can be linked to incidents around the fall of Srebrenica. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, we've become aware in this case of efforts by your unit to obtain further information and clarification from the Bosnian Ministry of Defence as to persons that were named on your missing list who may be registered as soldiers. Can you please tell us what was the event that alerted the demographics unit to check to see if there were any fallen soldiers of the ABiH among the Srebrenica missing, and when did that occur?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is not that I recall the actual event that made us look for this information, but seeing the age distribution and sex distribution of the Srebrenica missing, of course, it calls for attention for this particular issue. So at some point, intensive efforts were made to cross-reference the missing persons from Srebrenica with the military records that were available at the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were these intensive efforts begun in the year 2008 during the course of the Popovic trial?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't agree with that. It was much sooner than that. But in the Popovic trial, indeed this issue was raised by the Defence and certain activities have been redone again in that particular year.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you consider the military records of the ABiH that are within the possession of the Ministry of Defence to be a reliable data source, demographically speaking?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is a source that cannot be used to compile a list of victims because certain important pieces of information are missing there, like place of death is unavailable, or circumstances of death are also unavailable. So it is a limited information. Moreover, these list represent exits from ongoing registration of military personnel and other personnel related to the militaries from the point of view of whether or not they are alive or perhaps dead or they went missing. And, as such, as every dynamic registration of this kind, there are certain deficiencies in this lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do the ABiH records of fallen soldiers have JMBG unique identification numbers for these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to 65 ter number 06101.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we wait for that to come on the screen, I can say that this is a memo dated 16 May 2008 from Arve Hetland through you and Mr. Treanor to Mr. McCloskey. After you take a look at this, can you confirm for us if this would be the first report from your unit regarding overlap found on the ABiH fallen soldiers list with the 2005 Srebrenica missing list?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with certainty that this is the first memo. I am sure there were other memoranda on that. It is just a memo that -- yeah, at some point reported the findings from previous years, so this number was seen as very small at that time. Yeah, the numbers of militaries on the OTP lest.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look together at the second paragraph from the top. It is recorded there as follows: "Overall, 313 records on the 2005 OTP list were found on the ABiH list; i.e., 313 persons on the OTP list were reported as soldiers or other military personnel at some stage. Of those 313 records, 198 records reflected inconsistent dates of death/disappearance; i.e., dates falling outside the period considered relevant to the fall of Srebrenica." Was this the first time that there was clarification sought for personnel that had inconsistent dates of death or disappearance by the Office of the Prosecutor by your unit from the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- not the first time. Because, you know, in the same memo, in the third paragraph from the top, you have a mention that in 2004 there was an RFA concerning ABiH list, a RFA from the OTP to the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina. So it was not the first time. It was already 2004 that there were inconsistencies found in the context of ABiH records, that they were addressed to the authorities for clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we now take a look at D00344 in e-court together.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is dated just two months later. When it comes up on the screen, we'll see it's dated the 24th of July, 2008, and it is authored by you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for the record, I'd like to note that this is a MFI exhibit, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's possible. As a matter of fact, that's correct. I remember examining another witness on this and saying we'll wait for Ms. Tabeau to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, madam, looking at this document, it would appeared to be authored by you, and it would appear that the Popovic trial team urged your unit to take another look and compare the ABiH list with your list of missing. First of all, looking at this document, do you remember the circumstances of you authoring the same?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The circumstances. What do you mean by "circumstances"?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember being asked to take another look at the matching between the ABiH list and your list of missing based upon a request of the Popovic et al trial team.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, again, the inconsistencies, I think, between the military records and the basic information about the fall of Srebrenica, like the date and these kind of things, as far as I remember. The Defence was raising this issue intensively in the Popovic case, so it was actually part of the response to the claims that the Defence made in the Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, looking at the middle of the page, am I reading this right that using the indirect approach you were able to match 3.406 ABiH records and that using the direct approach you matched 4.964 ABiH records? Would those be matches with the list of missing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is about the matching with the census, I think. Sorry, through the census, with the Srebrenica list, you are right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the matching went through the census, so the fallen soldiers lists were made -- were matched with the census on the first place, in the first case, right? Yeah. And in the second case, yeah, it was a direct matching approach. Direct, that means military lists were matched directly with the Srebrenica victims list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And than would be the 4.964?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the memo we just looked at from two months prior had only 313 matches, now we have a figure of 4.964.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection. The -- at the bottom of the page we see that number, so it's just citing to part of the memo without the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not quite clear whether there's an objection to the question or to the circumstances under which it is put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I just wanted the witness to have the benefit of seeing the entire memo so that the question would not misrepresent the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, why don't we make it easier. Why don't we look at the -- the last paragraph on this page, and it will be the first completion of that paragraph on the next page that reads as follows: "An additional group of matches was obtained for the ABiH records from all regions other than Tuzla. Here, only 313 matches were produced. Many of them were the same as these included in," if we can turn the page, "5.273, but 98 matches were new. So, the overall total of matches of BiH records with the OTP list became 5.371. This comprises about 70 per cent of the OTP list."

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I recall this. And these results are part of the 2009 integrated report. There is an annex in the integrated report which is Annex 6, A6.4, which refers to the matching results of the military lists with Srebrenica list. So at the time when I was writing this memo, I also undertook a review of all the sources that were underlying the military records from especially the Tuzla region. Tuzla region is the main region from which the ABiH soldiers reported missing from Srebrenica - so obviously we -- we see it from the 2009 report - were registered. And it -- in -- in -- obviously a large part of information from the Tuzla region was earlier not used in the work of the Demographic Unit. It was related to the fact that a summary of -- a summary table provided to us by the authorities for Tuzla, the summary was incomplete. If all the subsequent subregions were taken one by one and put together, a different summary would emerge, a summary that included many more military individuals listed. So for my memo I used this reviewed data set from the Tuzla and obviously found many more matches between the Srebrenica victims and the military records. So this 70 per cent of the missing persons on the OTP list is the result obtained from these reviewed procedure -- reviewed data that was used for matching.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the question was unclear to me, because you started asking us to look at the only 313 matches and now having something in the area of 5.000. And then there was an objection but what exactly -- because then you read a portion of the document to the witness, and then she started her answer, Yes, that is true, apparently referring to the memo. Now it is unclear to me what exactly your question in this respect was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My question was going to be that the 313 needed to be added to this figure at the -- we had at the top, 4.964, to get to the final number which now we have linked all of that together, so that the 313 was not the totality of matches that they had at the beginning. It was totality of matches from regions other than Tuzla, other military archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now this question, to some extent may have been answered but not in full or has it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think now it has been answered. The doctor can perhaps assist me. If I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I accurately --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I -- I -- probably you are right, but it is also possible that these 313 are comprised in this bigger number, 5.000 something, produced from the review data set. But it might be -- there is also another aspect of this situation that the 70 per cent is quite a old number. It was based on the matches obtained from July 2008 ICMP records, I think, eventually. Well, I'm now moving through missing persons to the ICMP records, because this package that is coming together, one aspect of the problem is how many of the missing are at the same time reported as militaries. This is one aspect. Second aspect of this situation is how many of those militaries found on the OTP list are, at the same time, reported among the ICMP DNA identifications, and what is the link for them with the information about the graves. Are those graves mass graves, surface remains or other graves? So, of course, it is a fact that at least 70 per cent of the missing persons on the OTP missing persons list are militaries, because they are reported in the military records. But, at the same time, a very large number of them have been found identified through the DNA analysis by the ICMP and are linked to certain grave-sites available from the exhumation records. So that -- that -- these are the facts and this is all I can tell about it. Regarding numbers, these numbers are not final, that is my conclusion. And this is the answer to the question of the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could focus on the last paragraph of page 2 and then also on the first part of the next page, it ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're still dealing with the same memo, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which was assigned as D344 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MFI'd on the 20th of August of this year, and it was announced that it would be dealt with with Ms. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Looking at the last paragraph on the page, it says: "A total of 220 ABiH records for those matched (5.371) with the OTP list have inconsistent DOD. A complete overview of the 220 inconsistent cases is attached in Annex 2 to this memorandum. Of the 220 inconsistent cases," if we go on the next page, "140 have been confirmed as identified and related to Srebrenica grave-sites by the ICMP (according to the July 2008 update); 127 have been corrected by the FBH Ministry of Defence in 2003 in response to the OTP request for clarification of a number of inconsistent ABiH records identified by DU prior to and in the course of 2003; the corrected DODs and additionally provided PODs clearly point to the fact that these were all Srebrenica victims." Now the first question I have for you is in relation to this memorandum and the findings contained therein. Do they -- does it provide a complete picture of your unit's analysis of the matching between the ABiH lists and the Srebrenica missing list as well as the findings as of 2008?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes. These 220 inconsistent cases of which a large number have been already sorted out and there was still an outstanding number of 38 cases to be clarified at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With -- with respect to this memo, has there been any subsequent memo authored either by you or by someone else in your unit giving more complete data or information about this particular topic?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not anymore. Not that I recall. So the actual -- this analysis is where it stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because, actually, the unit stopped functioning at some point because of subsequent departures from the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you stand by the conclusions that you have in this document?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes. Well, if a new update would be made right now of the military records with the ICRC records of missing persons, I don't think the results would have been different, largely remain the same. I -- I don't think there would be much new things here. There would be quite some new information if we would do -- if I would do the matching of the military records on the OTP list with the ICMP data. So this number, 140 cases, mentioned here, as -- at that time confirmed in the ICMP records of DNA identifications, this number certainly would have been higher if the analysis would be done right now. That simply means that more inconsistent cases could be clarified by matching with the DNA identification, and a larger overlap would be available between the ICMP and military records just increasing the 70 per cent -- 73 per cent, actually, of the military records from the OTP lists confirmed to be identified by DNA analysis. It would be higher percentages these days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, based upon the foundation now laid with this witness, I would ask for D00344 MFI to be admitted as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar. Yes, the number is known already, so it is for me to -- to tell you that D344 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And one other item. I don't know whether the list is also one that should be under seal. I note that there is an annex that appears to be a list of names. That perhaps should be under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes. Because many are just identifications, DNA identifications that always remain a Rule 70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the admission is under seal. Was it MFI'd under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't remember. I don't have any notes as to that, and I just saw the list now when I had a hard copy of it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I may be of assistance, it was MFI'd as a public document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which -- well, we can't change that any further. It was MFI'd. It is now admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, let me just have a look. I see a list starting on page 4. Let me have a look. Annex 2 gives names of individuals. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, therefore, it's admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We'll get back to the inconsistent cases in a little bit. I'd like to first ask about the efforts to match with the ABiH lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based upon your knowledge and information, doctor, what about members of the civilian police in Srebrenica? Did you seek any records as to casualties among the civilian police members to perform matching with the Srebrenica missing list?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian police, you mean the defence -- Territorial Defence members or what -- well, in any case -

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Civilian police, Ministry of Internal Affairs, or MUP?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: MUP, yes. The military lists contain records of soldiers but also of police members and also the person, the civilian person, and of the ministries of the defence as well. So in this sense, this group is covered by the military records.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What about paramilitary formations or criminal groups? Did you have any data as to whether those were included amongst the ABiH lists or would they be in addition to?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- I don't think that military records cover paramilitaries. But, well, at least there is no category indicated in the data that paramilitaries are covered in the source.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's take a step --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I have to understand your last answer to be that even where paramilitary may have been registered or that criminals may have been registered as being members of the -- of the military that they do not appear as such in the military records.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are not flagged in the data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't simply know. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the lists of fallen soldiers from the ABiH that were received from the Ministry of Defence and used by your unit, do you know if these were generated according to official records of the ABiH or according to other statistical sources?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am not sure what is the meaning of official records of the ABiH. That means army records? These lists that I used were actually compiled in military units and partly at the Ministry of Defence, and at some point they were centralised, the ministries -- the Ministry of Defence. And I received this -- a copy of the central -- centralised list directly from the Ministry of Defence. I don't think I -- I -- I cannot think how different they would be from the official military records. It is the registration at the military unit level, in military regions, then subsequently to the central level, Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in your July 2008 memo that we just looked at, it was identified that at that time 127 had been corrected where dates of death and PODs, places of death, or disappearance had been corrected. If that is the case, then we have a number of soldiers which were registered as having a date of disappearance pre-dating the fall of Srebrenica and a -- in the years of 1994 or earlier, and some had different places. Would the fact that these records changed after the Prosecution sought more information, would that be a cause for concern in terms of the reliability of the confirmations so received?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we need to remember that these are records of missing persons largely. So that they are reported on military lists doesn't change the fact that they are reported as missing. And, as such, for missing persons, different dates can be reported as to when they were seen last time. And it doesn't contradict the fact that after reviewing a case, that the eventual data of going missing is later in time. And, as I said, this is a very -- this psychodynamic register, these are excerpts from a register that were provided to us at some point. It was around the year 2000 or so. So later in time it is possible that information was updated by additional facts about the persons. So it is possible that the dates were corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, madam, we're talking about corrections of some of the dates for 1992, 1993, and 1994. Does it cause concern for you that after clarifications was sought these dates miraculously changed to 1995. Doesn't it seem illogical that persons who are registered to have disappeared in 1992, 1993, 1994, according to military records from their specific units, could have just drastic changes or corrections in the date of disappearance or death?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the same time we must remember the same individuals were reported to the ICRC using the exact time frame of the fall of Srebrenica and the places related to the fall of Srebrenica. So there is another source, different than the military registration, that is telling us the same individuals disappeared in the context of the fall of Srebrenica. So drastic or not, the corrections made sense, and, of course, my assumption was that the authorities who provided these clarifications and indicated that the dates of disappearance should be different had a foundation for these clarifications. They just didn't make it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the time the clarification was sought, did the Prosecution let the Ministry of Defence know that these persons were on the Srebrenica missing list or had been found exhumed in mass graves?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you -- you are certainly familiar with the RFA format the OTP has been using over the years, reference is made in RFAs to a particular case for which the Prosecution is seeking clarification. So if the case name was mentioned like Popovic, for instance, or other Srebrenica relate case, even to this fact the authorities knew, of course, about the circumstances of this missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems to me that there may be some misunderstanding as the gist of the question. I do understand but, please correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Ivetic, that you would like to hear from Ms. Tabeau that when the RFA was sent, whether information was sent at the same time about individuals that had been found exhumed in mass graves. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: More concerned with whether the individuals for whom the clarification were sought were identified by the OTP as being persons on their list of missing. To say in essence, We have information that these men were missing in Srebrenica, could you clarify. And if that's the clarification that was sought or if it was a more neutral or generic request sought [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are -- your concern may be that the Prosecution more or less invited --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the authorities to move the disappearance from the earlier years to 1995, because they would have suggested that in their request.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Right. Unintentionally or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm phrasing it as neutrally as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall exactly the wording. In my view, we never try -- we always try to avoid to give this kind of information in request for clarification. But I think it is very easy to check the text of the RFAs. My initial answer would be we just don't do this in RFAs. We provide request for clarification and we would provide a list of names and request details of the date of death and place of death or disappearance for a number of individuals listed on the military lists. I don't think we shared information about identification and graves for these individuals. For sure not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And also not information that triggered the need for verification; that is, This is what you told us, but we found the person in a grave in -- near Srebrenica. That is more suggestive than just saying, Could you please find out whether the date of birth was correct or whether it needs to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I -- I would believe we tend to skip all the indications, possible indications. But we would mention that because of inconsistencies found in a given list there is a need to check and clarify this and that. But, as I'm saying, we can refer to the actual RFAs. But this has been the practice of the office and of my unit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, it seems that the RFA would be accessible. Is there any way you would like to have it in to evidence? I mean, apparently you find it relevant.
