The witness says she doesn't have a clear recollection on it but only on what they usually did. I take it that Ms. Marcus would be glad to provide --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have been working with Ms. Marcus to locate the RFAs for, I think, a couple of weeks now, and I don't know whether we still have a full set of all the RFAs. We're finding one or two at a time or several at a time. So I would defer to Ms. Marcus as to whether the RFAs that she and I have discussed are the totality of the RFAs in relation to this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first -- yes. First things, of course, is the RFA which triggered the correction. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We have provided and discussed with Mr. Ivetic, as he says, 15 different RFAs and responses. If Mr. Ivetic identifies for us which one of these he would like to tender, I would -- I don't think we would have a problem with tendering any of them if it is relevant to the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, the Chamber is not seeking to have -- to be overloaded with material which is available. But if apparently you consider this to be important, so you could you please identify, together with Ms. Marcus, which RFA is the relevant one so that we could have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can. I'll identify those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the Chamber appreciates that you sat together to try to find out what RFAs had been produced. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can at this time call up but not broadcast number 25876. Actually, let's -- let's go into private session. It will make it easier for purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In relation to the methodology that you employed when using the voter lists to determine population size and ethnicity, am I correct that you would take a name from the voter list and try to match it to a name on a census list and then determine the ethnicity or nationality by the basis of what is reported in the census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ethnicity was reported on the basis of the census.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The other week you testified about there being 91 different ways of expressing nationality in the former Yugoslavia at the time of the 1991 census. For purposes of your study, did you keep all 91 nationalities as expressed in the census or did you convert some by assigning a nationality based upon the name of the individual, a technique similar to that you used in Mostar for the Prlic case?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't use names to assign ethnicity to individuals. The three major ethnic groups, the Muslim, Serbs and Croats, were taken as reported in the census records, and the remaining ethnicities, being mainly Yugoslavs or mixed ethnicities, Serbo-Croat, for instance, Croat-Serb, other nationalities like German, these other than different -- the three main groups were taken jointly under the name of others.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now in relation to the work reviewing the voter register, did you at any point in time have access to any publications or manuals published by the OSCE talking about the unreliability of the names as recorded in the voter databases?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OSCE maintains a web site where they include many reports that are produced by the organisation, manuals, et cetera. So these documents can be easily downloaded and studied. But I don't recall that there were documents that I was studying relating to names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if I may just interrupt -- Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, Mr. Ivetic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Again, Madam Tabeau, at -- at page 32, starting from lines 22, to page 33, line 2, you're talking about the three main groups, Serbs, Bosniaks, and Croats. And then you listed the number of smaller little groups, at the end of which you then said: "... other nationalities like German, these other than different -- the three main groups were taken jointly under the name of others." Did you many to say the three main groups, meaning Serb-Croat and Bosniak or did you mean these smaller groups were taken as others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, the smaller groups were taken as others and the three main groups were taken separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Each separately as one ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The record is corrected. Thank you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we can turn to 1D1441 briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we wait for that, I can introduce it as a handbook issued by the OSCE to its staff working on the 1997 voter lists. And once we have both versions, if we can turn to page 2 in both versions. At the very top of the same, we have this notation. It says: "Very important: Due to a large number of incorrectly written names in the database, it is best to use just the first few letters of the last name followed by an asterix." Were you a ware that the OSCE considered the database they were using had a large number of incorrectly written names?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall I was speaking about it shortly last week that the voters' register of 1997 was actually based on the 1991 census. So these are the names from the census we are talking about. And, yes, of course, many names from the census contained all kind of inconsistencies, spelling mistakes and misformed characters, because the computerised version of the census was obtained through optical scanning. During the scanning process, many characters became misshaped. And, actually, my unit spent a lot of time and effort on correcting and improving the names, including making -- bridging tables between the misshaped names and corrected names. The corrected names were obtained from a review process in which native speakers, B/C/S speakers, were intensively involved. So the misshaped characters were replaced by characters that were correct. Also a computer programme was used that was detecting impossible combinations of letters, impossible in the B/C/S language, and the impossible combinations again were replaced by possible combinations, most likely combinations. Also a household correction method was used. Names within every household were checked, surnames, of course, on the first place, and differences within households were studied. If they were differently spelled names within a given household, they were corrected by taking the name that was spelled correctly. So a lot of effort was done in my unit to correct the names and the names have been corrected in both, the 1991 census and also voters' registers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have a statistic or percentage for the proportion of the names that had to be corrected by personnel of the Office of the Prosecutor in order to permit a match?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- I -- I can tell you approximately that the number of corrections of names was like 500.000. But I wouldn't tell these -- that these were the corrections necessary to obtained as one match. These were the corrections that were needed in order to engage seriously in the matching process and obtain as many matches as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was 500.000 upon a total of ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Out of the census, 4.4 million records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So close to anywhere between 10 and 15 per cent.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do we know in relation to the names reported in, let's say, the Srebrenica list of missing how many of those had to be corrected from the way that they were recorded in either the census or the voters records?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I cannot tell how many Srebrenica related victims have corrected names. But when I was talking about the corrections in the census and the voters, right, that is how you addressed the issue. I don't recall that a significant number of names were corrected on the ICRC list of missing persons from Srebrenica. Although there will be spelling differences between the ICRC list and the census list, of course, there will be. But correcting this one way to deal with the differences, another way of dealing with differences is allowing for some spelling differences of one and the same name, like, you know, matching based on 75 per cent consistency of characters in a given name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Ivetic wanted to know whether the percentage of names that had to be corrected was, percentage-wise, higher in the Srebrenica selected population. I should say, the -- the victims lists. And I would like to add to that, that if you would not know, whether there's any reason to believe that such mistakes were more frequent in the -- whether there is any indication that they would be more frequent than elsewhere in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So my answer would be they wouldn't be more frequent because we are talking about optical scanning as the source for the differences in -- and misshaping of characters and that's no reason to believe that the optical scanning was selective and was more higher in the case of Srebrenica victims than in case of any other individual listed in the census. So, no, no particular bias for Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, for purposes of your work, which relied upon the 1991 census, do you have concrete figures for how many people participated in the 1991 census and then left voluntarily for work or other reasons thereafter?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Um, I think we -- we did a study of the population living abroad that was registered in the 1991 census, and the results of this study are reported, I think, in the annex to the Slobodan Milosevic report. I wouldn't recall a number, but I don't think it was a very high number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we've had evidence at this trial that persons began leaving Srebrenica in 1993 already, and, in fact that they had been evacuated by the UN at that time. We have, for instance, Mr. Butler at transcript page 16193 through 16194. Did you have that kind of information or knowledge at the time that you were doing your reports?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any source that would be listing the population movements from Srebrenica before the fall of Srebrenica, and you are talking about 1993. Not -- not that I had a list of names of these persons. Except for perhaps a broader database that was, I think, submitted to the OTP at some point around 1997, I guess, as far as I remember. These were lists of -- of refugee, Srebrenica refugees, so I guess there would be a number of them reported as having left Srebrenica already in the years like 1993. So there was such a list, indeed. But I didn't use this list, for many reasons, including, on the first place, the incompleteness of the reporting; and, second, that a better source on the IDPs and refugees was also available in my unit, which is the so-called DDPR registration of IDPs and refugees that completed -- that included match -- more completed information about internal displacement and refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the number and boundaries of the Srebrenica municipality and bordering municipalities have changed since 1991?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some case, they did. Actually, for quite a number of municipalities, the Dayton Agreement proposed a new division between the Federation and Republika Srpska, so a number of municipalities became split municipalities with two parts, instead of one bigger municipality. But Srebrenica itself is not one of the split municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What geographic region did you use to define the Srebrenica municipality for purposes of your report and study?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can read in the first annex to the 2009 report that the Srebrenica area comprised actually ten municipalities, as far as I can remember. Actually, it is Annex 2, page 34. And these are municipalities including Bijeljina, Bratunac, Han Pijesak, Kalesija, Kladanj, Rogatica, Sekovici, Srebrenica, Vlasenica and Zvornik. And also areas in the bordering territory with Serbia, Bajina Basta, Ljubovija and Valjevo were considered relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And those last three are on the territory -- are part of Serbia proper; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the PHR lists and the ICRC list, can you tell us what percentage of corrections did you have to undertake in relation to those sources to obtain a match and what criteria were utilised? Do you have any records of that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- I -- I don't -- I can't tell you statistics. That is one thing, and, well, corrections are a part of a regular process. Any source received in the demographic unit were subject to cleaning, to checking inconsistency, identifying problems, and correcting problems if the problems could be corrected. So, for instance, things like reformatting dates reported in all kinds of formats or correcting names, this was part of a regular process. So it is not that I can link these corrections and cleaning - I would call it cleaning and reformatting - of sources with particular numbers of matches obtained later.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Specifically for the work on Srebrenica, were you able to utilise as a data source the official registries of recorded deaths; that is to say, were these sources that could have been used understanding that you did not use them?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official death notifications you are referring to, those --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]

utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll do my best. The final matter I would like to address Your Honours in relation to Dr. Tabeau's testimony relates to the proof of death documentary evidence that the Prosecution seeks to tender from the bar table in the connection with Dr. Tabeau's evidence. With this motion, the Prosecution seeks admission of the documents used in the POD annex, P2797, from the bar table. The Prosecution is in the process of preparing the final list of those documents, conducting yet another review to ensure that the selection is as stream-lined as possible. As the POD documents share the same basis of relevance and probative value, we make this submission to tender the documents. We will provide the Chamber and the Defence with the final list as soon as possible. As I believe Your Honours may have understood from the expert evidence of Dr. Tabeau, proving the deaths of victims of charged incidents in this case differs incident by incident, depending upon many factors, including, the manner in which the victims were killed, where they were buried, whether there were exhumations, and whether there is witness evidence. For a many of the non-Srebrenica incidents, there have been no exhumations and no DNA identifications. For other incident, there were exhumations and autopsies but no DNA identifications, rather classical identifications. In many cases there were numerous alleges, both national and international, involved in the exhumations, autopsies, identifications, producing a varied body of evidence. As Dr. Tabeau explained during her testimony, the war situation in which much of this evidence was gathered, has resulted in a collection of evidence which must be analysed as a whole in order to determine the fate of the named victims. The Prosecution's evidence in relation to the named victims comprises three components: Witness evidence is the first, for the most part already adduced; Dr. Tabeau's analysis and conclusions in her POD expert report and the annex is the second; and the third is the body of documentary evidence relating to the deaths of the named victims, which the Prosecution is now tendering. The Prosecution will be relying on these three evidentiary groups taken together as a whole in order to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that a particular named victim was a victim of a specific incident with which the accused has been charged in the indictment. As Your Honours could appreciate during the testimony of Dr. Tabeau, for example, when we analysed the evidence relating to 6-year-old Almina Keranovic, even taking Dr. Tabeau's evidence at its highest, without the actual documents in evidence, the Chamber might have been left curious as to how certain information was gathered and how conclusions were drawn in the POD annex which analyses these documents. The Prosecution submits that these documents are all relevant to the fate of the specific victim they refer to and will provide significant assistance to the Chamber in considering all the evidence available when determining the fate of the named victims of the charged crimes. The Prosecution will thus be providing in the near future a list of approximately 1.400 documents that are used in the POD annex as sources analysed to determine the fate of the victims. The list will, of course, not include the POD documents that have already been admitted nor will it conclude -- include the 261 documents that were tendered in our bar table motion of the 31st of October. We are in the process of organising the documents in a very clear manner incident by incident and victim by victim to facilitate their review in tandem with the POD annex of the Tabeau report. The Prosecution is mindful of the number of these documents. However, we are also mindful of the large number of victims of the crimes with which Mr. Mladic has been charged. There are tens of thousands of victims of the crimes charged in the indictment, yet the Prosecution's filed victim lists for the municipalities and Sarajevo contains approximately 1.450 names. Further, Dr. Tabeau has identified in her analysis approximately 740 additional named victims, bringing the total number of victims to be specifically named in this case to approximately 2.200. I emphasise the word "named," Your Honours, because the named victims do not make up the entirety of the victim group. They are, in fact, but a fraction of the total number of victims of these crimes. The Prosecution thus submits that considering the number of victims charged in this case, less than one document per named victim is, in fact, a very modest stream-lined body of evidence. In judgements at international tribunals and courts, often there are either no named victims or very few named victims. There is most often no forensic evidence of any kind available to prove the deaths of the victims. This Prosecution team views it as its duty to make effective use of the remarkable amount of documentary evidence available relating to the victims' deaths. The Prosecution views the unnamed victims as akin to those buried in unmarked graves. Place holders for individuals who may be victims of crimes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour. We view them as place holders for individuals who may be victims of crimes ultimately attributed to the accused, but who, due to an absence of evidence of their identities, cannot be named. The Prosecution view is that, to the extent that we are able to prove - and the Chamber is able to find - beyond a reasonable doubt that an individual named person is a victim of a crime attributed to the accused, that person and their surviving family members deserve for their daughter, brother, mother, and sister, to be named as a victim in the final judgement. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.text: Is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'd note, we've also uploaded a redact version, 65 ter 30184A, which I would tender as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the system here is that they should not be tendered, but let's review that, that they should be filed at a later stage rather than become then for the second time part of the body of evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm entirely in Your Honours' hands as to that. I'd ask next that the Court Officer call up 65 ter 11012.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, what we're seeing here is a report. It has your name at the bottom, the date 27 November 1992. Can you describe for us --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 2002. I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you describe for us the scope and purpose of this report?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Your Honours, when I arrived at the ICTY I was tasked with exploiting a series of documents from the 1st Krajina Corps archive. When I started working on that material, there were documents which were of interest to the investigative teams but I also felt that potentially as a whole they might form the basis of an analytical report that would, first and foremost, give me an understanding of the operations of the 1st Krajina Corps, but then later, Ms. Joanna Korner, who is Senior Trial Attorney, felt that it would be useful to have as part of her work a more comprehensive report on the activities of the 1st Krajina Corps in the Bosanska Krajina in 199.2 and that's when the report was tasked. I set the framework for the report. I utilised predominantly documents from the 1st Krajina Corps archive along with some other police documents and some political documents and a smaller number of open-source materials. But that, in general, is the background to the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you describe the limitations of the report, if any.

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, the report is limited. It's limited in terms of its time. It predominantly deals with 1992. There are some references in 1993, if they reflect back on activity in 1992. The document predominantly deals with materials from the 1st Krajina Corps archives, so contemporaneous documents from that military structure. Obviously within that archive there are other document from other locations such as the Main Staff or from lower level brigade units, for example. But it is documentary based, and so it doesn't deal with other types of sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that 65 ter 11012 be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar the number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 11012 receives number P2859, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2859 is admitted -- is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I ask that the Court Officer call up 65 ter 20003.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As this comes up, sir, I understand over the years two errata sheets to the Krajina report have been put together. When it comes up, I'll just ask you to look at the screen and tell us is this one of those sheets.

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: This one is, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'd ask that that be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 20003 receives number P2860, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 11000.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, is this the other such sheet?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'd ask that this be marked for identification as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have a translation for it? Because we see on our left screen -- yes. There seems to be -- no, as a matter of fact, they're both in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll check that over the course of the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's then a second reason to have it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 11000 receives number P2861, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification but not for the reason any further that there's no B/C/S translation because there seems to be one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I won't specify who, Your Honour, but it's been corrected very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask that the Court officer --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, before I do that. Is there one additional correction to this report that footnote 41 refers in fact to parts of two documents, one from April 28th and one from May 2nd?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask that the Court Officer call up 65 ter 30188.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this report?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can you describe, again, the scope and purpose for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: I believe in late 2012 I was asked by the trial team, Mr. Groome, in particular, if I would consider doing a report on the subject here which is Manjaca detention camp. That report I agreed to do, and the tasking was slightly expanded too to give a contextual analysis to the -- to the report in relation to the VRS Main Staff as well. So that report was requested, I believe, in November 2012 and it was completed by me in March 2013.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did it refer as well to additional material beyond the 1st Krajina Corps collection?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it did. In part, it also contains a number of documents which were also in the 1st Krajina Corps or other documents, but I was provided with documents from Manjaca camp, a number of which form the basis of this document -- these were documents that I hadn't seen before in writing the Krajina report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask that this document be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30188 receives number P2862, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask that the Court Officer call up 65 ter 30467.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Does it reflect your comments on various other documents?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. This was a statement I gave when asked to comment on documents I hadn't used for the Krajina Corps report but had come into the possession of the OTP since then. At that time I was -- I was no longer working within the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Have you reviewed the statement in preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you still hold the opinions reflected herein?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And having taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm that the statement truthfully and correctly records your opinions?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this also be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number of the statement would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30467 receives number P2863, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, because of the nature of the statement, I suggest not to do a Rule 92 ter summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That -- the public will understand what the testimony of this witness is about, even when no summary is read. Therefore, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I hope so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning, then, back to your review of the documents in the 1st Krajina Corps archive, did any patterns arise from your review of those documents?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. And I believe a number of those are -- are laid out in the -- the report itself. Some of those patterns include, for example, a convergence between the JNA and the SDS in the spring of 1992, the moving back of some units from Western Slavonia in 5th Corps zone back to municipalities in the Krajina, patterns in relation to disarmament operations, and some patterns in relation to the seizing control of municipalities in the Krajina in -- the spring of 1992. But a number of the other patterns are laid out in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll just ask you about a couple of those. The report describes linkage between military operations and strategic objectives at, for instance, page 5. Is that one of the patterns that emerged for you?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was one of the issues that seemed to raise itself from the review and materials in the document that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Since you drafted the Krajina report, you've reviewed a large number of additional documents, including General Mladic's notebooks. I will ask you about certainly of those as we go on, but for now I have a simple question: Has your review of those addition documents altered or reinforced your conclusions as to the patterns of events described in the Krajina report?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: I don't think the -- the review of the additional materials that I have seen has necessarily altered the underlying conclusions in the report. And, in fact, in many areas, the documents have added and reinforced the conclusions. So I -- I don't think it changes much, but I think what it does is given additional weight to some of those conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask the Court Officer call up Exhibit P02367.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For efficiency and because we have limited time, I will sometimes direct your attention to particular portions of a document. However, for clarity, I'll start with an example and ask you to help us understand the document. First, this document is dated June 1st, 1992. Can you give us a sense of what has been happening in the 1st Krajina Corps' area of responsibility right before that date?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. This is an example of a daily combat report that the 1st Krajina Corps sent to the Main Staff. It actually is a report that didn't change in terms of format when the 5th Corps or the JNA transformed into the 1st Krajina Corps. All that changed was that the distribution to the Main Staff changed. At this time, the 5th Corps has renamed itself -- sorry, the 1st Krajina Corps has renamed itself to the 1st Krajina Corps and there have been a number of municipality operations in and around the Krajina at this time which the corps was involved in and which it's reporting in this daily combat report. It also makes mention that a large number of prisoners have been taken as part of these operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Traldi, if I may just interrupt. Mr. Brown, the record says that the Krajina Corps has renamed itself to the 1st -- the 1st Krajina Corps has renamed itself to the 1st Krajina Corps. Is that all you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I meant to say the 5th Corps. It was the JNA 5th Corps prior to this, then it became the 1st Krajina Corps after the transition into the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we turn to page 2 in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting at this moment. But I don't see this document on the list proposed with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As always, Mr. Lukic, the list for an expert witness includes clearly on the list reference to all of the exhibits in the expert witness's report. This one, for instance, is cited at footnote 619 of the Krajina report. And in our e-mail sending out the list, I don't have the exact language in front of me, but we referred to the annex to our 92 ter filing setting out those exhibits by footnote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it's used as an example rather than ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In this case, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in this case. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One more thing. I don't know, maybe I don't have the right version, but on my version of 65 ter list there is no sentence that would indicate that materials from the expert report would be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd refer Mr. Lukic to our e-mail of November 11th at 5.50. It's in my copy of the list as well. But, of course, I don't have his copy. The last sentence on page 2. Sorry, page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll try to find that one. Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have page 3 in the B/C/S, actually, 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Here it refers to mopping up operations under clause 8. Do you see that language?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll come to those operations more later. But if -- at this time can you provide us with a general sense of the consequences for non-Serbs of what are referred to as mopping up activities?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: At the time of writing of this document, units of the 1st Krajina Corps had been involved in operations in the municipalities mentioned in section 8. And they had taken control of those municipalities, often resulting in the movement out and capturing of detainees from non-Serb villages. And this reference would seem to indicate that they're continuing this process and continuing to mop up those particular areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 3 in the English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is that a 1st Krajina Corps stamp or a 5th Corps stamp?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: It's annotated as a 5th Corps stamp. This was probably because the transition between the 5th Corps and the 1st Krajina Corps had only been a few weeks before this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem. Mr. Stojanovic, could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you check with Mr. Mladic what his problem is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honours. Mr. Mladic has asked me to ask the Prosecutor to slow down because he is unable to follow the discussion at this pace. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, that's a clear request not only from the interpreters but also from the accused to slow down. Would you please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I will. I'd ask that the Court Officer call up 65 ter 16492.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And for your reference, sir, I'll start with some brief questions about the JNA 5th Corps. Can you tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: This is a hand-over certificate for the command of the JNA 5th Corps on the 19th of March, 1992, and a handing over to General Talic, who, up until that time, had been the deputy commander of the corps. He took command on this date. He remained the 5th Corps commander and the 1st Krajina Corps commander on establishment of the VRS and remained corps commander for the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tendered 65 ter 16492.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 16492 receives number P2864, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'd ask that the Court Officer call up 65 ter 28398. This is an order from the 5th Corps dated the 1st of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir, in your report, you describe a twin-track policy that the JNA was on at that time. Could you describe that for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, this is a -- near the beginning of my report when the documents indicated to me that in the early months of 1992, in -- in particular, in Bosnia, the situation was deteriorating, and the JNA were redeployed into areas in Bosnia with the intention -- or with the instruction of reducing ethnic tensions. And it would seem that that was a task that they were given, presumably in part because they wished Bosnia to remain as part of a federal -- within the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. So on the one hand there are those tasks, but there are other documents indicating that the JNA was providing weapons to the Bosnian Serbs, that it was siding very much with the position of the Bosnian Serbs. So, on the one hand, there was this policy of trying to reduce ethnic tensions, I would argue, in an attempt to maintain as much of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia as possible, and on the other hand and more covertly providing assistance to the Bosnian Serbs and their position. And that's where I think I would argue the twin-track policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This report refers to the 6th brigade and say it should be deployed in the Sanski Most area. Based on a your review of documents, was that carried out?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was moved back from Western Slavonia where it had been operating in combat operations there and it was moved back to Sanski Most at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In the next paragraph the document states: "Establish full co-operation with the organs of government in Sanski Most municipality and collaboration with TO and police units." Again, based on your review of documents, was this sort of co-operation between 5th Corps units and the civilian authorities implemented?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. And in the case of the 6th Brigade, in particular, it -- it was conducting this co-operation with organs on the ground, and later, very much so, when Crisis Staffs were established and, in fact, the brigade commander of this brigade was -- was very much an active member of the Crisis Staff in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say the Crisis Staff you're referring to the Bosnian Serb Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I am, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you relate that co-operation to what the 1st Krajina Corps was doing after the transformation of the JNA and the creation of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. And, in fact, immediately on the transition into the VRS on the 19th/20th of May, 1992, General Talic, as the corps commander, stressed this in a number of his documents and actively stressed that co-operation was to be expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe we had extended sessions this week but I'm happy to break now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're right, Mr. Traldi. I had forgotten that. Therefore please proceed for another half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would start by tendering this document as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28398 receives number P2865, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'd request now 65 ter 06586. It is a report of 12 May 1992 from the 5th Corps Command to the 2nd Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, I think the -- Madam Registrar mentioned the 65 ter of P2865 which doesn't appear on the transcript yet.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That was number 28398 that received number P2865, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As this document comes up, sir, thinking now of early May 1992 can you characterise the 5th Corps at that point in general terms?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: I'm not sure exactly the question. Are you talking about where it was deployed and what it was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's start with what it was doing.

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Part of the corps was withdrawing from Western Slavonia having been involved in operations there since that later part of 1991. Other parts were in municipalities within its zone of operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in terms of professionalism, can you express an opinion as to the 5th Corps?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: It was a corps that was quite seasoned. It had significant combat experience in Western Slavonia. It was led by a commander who had been involved in those operations -- a deputy commander and then a commander. It was a corps that had significant hardware and military hardware, armoured units, tank units, heavy artillery, and it was certainly an effective corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In this document, here on page 1 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S, the 5th Corps reports: "The Muslim and Croat population is moving out of the area of Donji Vakuf towards Bugojno." Can you explain the importance of that note in your view.

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Well, Donji Vakuf area was part of the 5th Corps zone, and it's evident that the 5th Corps at this time is acutely aware of what is going on there and that Muslims and Croats are leaving that area, and it is being reported up as a significant issue to the 2nd Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The document is dated 12 May. Who was in charge of the 2nd Military District at that time?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: General Mladic was in charge at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd tendered that document as the next public Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 06586 receives number P2866, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2866 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You described earlier a process of convergence between the JNA and Serb authorities. By this point, roughly 12 May, what was the status of that convergence process?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Basically in the first weeks of May 1992 there were a number of meetings, in essence to transform the JNA units left behind by the JNA in Bosnia into the VRS culminating on the 12th of May with the 16th Assembly Session and the announcement of the VRS, establishment of the army. So there had been discussions prior to this about the process of how that was going to happen, including with senior JNA officer, SDS leaders, and General Mladic in -- in -- in this case, who later became the head of the VRS, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you describe a process. How far down the road of that process were the JNA and the Bosnian Serbs by this point?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: By the 12th of May, I think this combat report - I'm not sure of the timing - but by the 12th of May, in essence, it had been announced that the VRS would be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll get to some of the meetings you describe in a moment. But before we do, you discussed the professionalism of the 5th Corps. In your Krajina report, paragraphs 1.67 to 1.69 you refer to portion of the VRS combat readiness report, Exhibit 338, which refers to two phases of development of the VRS. Did you see those phases in the Krajina Corps' area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I did, very much so. I think the combat analysis report indicates that the first phase was concerned with liberating municipality territories and the establishment of the Main Staff, and I believe that documentary references from that early part up until June very much reflect that -- reflected that in -- and the second phase is annotated as one where directives are used and -- and on -- wider strategic goals are implemented. But I saw that very much so in -- in the 5th Corps documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One of the other things that portion of the report discusses is the first phase being heavily consisting of locally organised units. Is that something that you saw in the 5th Corps' area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: In terms of locally organised units, no. There were TO units, mobilised TO units that were part of that process of taking over municipalities, yes. But in terms of the 5th Corps, many of the units that were involved were actually the same units that had been working in Western Slavonia. They were the formed units of the corps, so, for example, the 43rd Motorised Brigade was involved in Prijedor. We have just seen the document about the 6th Brigade in Sanski Most. They were the units that were also involved in the operations in the municipalities in May and June and later. So it wasn't, if you like, units that are outside of that -- that -- that corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask now that we have Exhibit P352, page 211 in the English, 213 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, what we're calling up now is one of General Mladic's notebooks. Have you studied those notebooks yourself?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I reviewed them as part of my testimony and I had reviewed them previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, can you give us the number of the exhibit again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. P352, page 211 in the English, and I believe it's 213 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This notebook entry records a meeting including, among others, Mladic and General Adzic on 30 April 1992. What importance do you attach to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: I think this meeting, in particular, is -- very much talks to this issue of convergence. The context, I think, behind this meeting was that obviously there had been a declaration of the new FRY, which was to only consist of Serbia and Montenegro, and so it put the JNA in a slightly difficult position in relation to its formations in Bosnia and also how that was going to affect the Bosnian Serbs within Bosnia. And this meeting on the 30th, General Adzic, who was the acting federal secretary for National Defence and Chief of Staff of the JNA, is explaining, I believe, that no matter what, the FRY, the new FRY, is something of a fait accompli, and it's negotiating how they can support the Bosnian Serbs from a military perspective if, as -- as -- as and when that technical JNA withdrawal occurs, which was to happen around the 19th, or middle of May. And what happens here is General Adzic suggests or says that -- that the JNA, in essence, would be -- will remain, there will be forces remaining in Serbian areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 224 in the English and 228 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Here, General Mladic records at the bottom of the English page: "Great damage," refers to Arkan in Bijeljina, the destruction of Foca, lootings and torchings, torching of Croatian villages at Kupres, bombardment of the old part of Sarajevo. What importance do you attach to this language?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Well, it would seem that General Mladic is -- is aware very much of the activities in those areas and the potential criminal activity that seems to be going on, in terms of looting and torching of villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 246 now, please, in the English; 250 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you give us a time-frame for the last portion we looked at, page 224?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The same meeting, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same meeting still.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Here, we see at the top of the page the date 5 May 1992. And it reflects some questions General Mladic has noted down. What importance do you ascribe to that, if any?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: I might have to go back to the 30th of August [sic]. But I believe later in that document Adzic lays out that they will be protecting the Serbs and that units will be moved back, or suggested that units will be moved back into Serb areas. And I think in between that meeting and here, the decision has clearly been taken that there's going to be a new -- that the -- that the -- the remnants of the JNA in Bosnia will form the basis of the new Bosnian Serb army. And I -- it would appear that on 5th May that General Mladic is noting down issues or aspects that need to be resolved in order for the VRS -- well, the new VRS, to be established and -- and points for discussions. So objectives, for example, the character of the army, relationship with the territory, relationship between non-Serbs and Serbian inhabitants, and all the other issues of -- the headquarters. So, in essence, it seems like a decisions that been taken that this is going to happen, and here are some of the issues that need resolution or discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the beginning of your answer, sir, you were recorded to refer to the 30th of August. Was that the date you meant to refer to?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: 30th of May I -- I apologise. Sorry, 30th April. The one we just realised at -- looked at, the Adzic meeting prior to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we turn to the next page, page 247 in the English, 251 in the B/C/S. In the middle, under 1330 hours, we see Mladic recording talks with General Adzic. Have you reviewed that discussion in preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you have any comment on the substance of this conversation?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Again, this is following on from the practical issues of establishing the VRS. If possible, I'd like to see the next section.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It -- it continues along this vein about -- discussions about how practically they're going to establish the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we turn to page 253. It's 258 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see the beginning of a meeting on 6 May. And there's a discussion of killings by SDS representatives in Bratunac. Turning to the next page in each version, Mladic records: "Send someone to Bratunac to calm them down."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be... No -- no loud speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Mladic, you may speak at low voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Below that if the B/C/S has -- the B/C/S appears to have come up, it writes: "Karadzic to send someone to pacify the extremists." What importance do you ascribe to this language?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: Could I see the previous page again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we go back to 253 in the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would seem, again, that General Mladic has received some briefing about the activities in Bratunac, which has included the killing of non-Serbs. And there is a reference to the TO there being involved, or inviting individuals in. It seems that the emphasis here is to try and calm the situation, rather than to investigate or even potentially prosecute anyone who may have conducted some kind of criminal act.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn, then, to the next page in the English. Sorry, I think my notes are in error and we should go one page further. And one page further in the B/C/S for Mr. Mladic as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Here we see a list of things to do. What importance do you ascribe to that list?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: I think this follows on in chronology concerning General Mladic's tasks or issues of -- to resolve in the establishment of the new VRS. It would seem to be that General Mladic here is already thinking about what tasks he needs to conduct or carry out in order to establish the headquarters and to ensure an effective military. So cleaning the commands of dead wood, presumably meaning getting rid of ineffective commanders. So it's a follow-on from the checklist earlier on, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning now to page 262 in the English; 270 in the transcript in B/C/S. We see the date, 7 May 1992, meeting, Krajisnik, and then it lays out a number of strategic -- of what are termed strategic goals. What importance do you attach to these?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: I think this is an important meeting in which one of the comments that General Mladic had noted earlier on about objectives were clearly discussed. In order to resolve this issue: What should the new army, or the VRS's, objectives be. Here Krajisnik lists them, and they are -- although there's seven here, they are very -- in fact, they are identical to the ones that were presented at the 16th Assembly Session on 12th of May. So, to me, this period - 5th, 6th, 7th of May - is about the establishment of the VRS and -- and -- and getting an idea of what the objectives of the VRS are to be. And, of course, they are publicly announced that -- or at least they're announced at the Assembly session a few days later. And if we go back to the Main Staff analysis readiness report, it makes mention that the -- the beginning of the VRS started in those early days of May, 1992, and this would seem to reflect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 264. That's page 272 in the B/C/S. Can you explain the diagram that's been recorded here.

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN
utterances.text: This is an annotation of the proposed new VRS. Again, this is this preliminary process of analysis and decision, and this would seem to be a structural diagram of what the -- what General Mladic expected the VRS or -- the VRS to be. And, indeed, this is very similar to what it became, although they added an extra corps later in 1992. So here you have annotation of the 1st Krajina Corps, (Banja Luka), that's why where the 5th Corps was. And this seems to be his wiring diagram, structural diagram of what the VRS is going to be in the preceding weeks -- days and weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point, I would turn to the 16th Assembly Session. I would imagine it would take us past the end time for today, and so for continuity, I'd suggest we might break a couple of minutes early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then do so. I'd like to instruct you, Mr. Brown, that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever, about your testimony. Whether that is testimony you have given already today, or that's testimony still to be given in the days to follow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 19th of November, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of November, 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
